metaData.originalTitle: When RAG Users Ask Vague Questions: Clarify Once， Learn the Default
metaData.title: When RAG Users Ask Vague Questions: Clarify Once， Learn the Default
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a pattern for handling vague user queries in RAG systems: ask one focused clarification, learn the default from the answer, and stay silent on subsequent similar questions.
metaData.summary: The article extends the question-parsing brick of an enterprise RAG system to handle ambiguous fields common in production queries. It identifies five failure modes (ambiguous field type, missing page scope, ambiguous date scope, ambiguous intent, implicit entity) and introduces two Pydantic schemas: `ClarificationRequest` to ask the user and `ClarificationDefault` to learn from the answer. A worked broker example demonstrates the loop: first time the system asks, records the answer, and later reuses the learned default silently. The update rules and gate function are provided in Python. The pattern is positioned as distinct from multi-turn dialogue; it emphasizes learning across requests rather than within a conversation. The article also discusses boundaries, deferred concerns (multi-field, adversarial users, cross-tenant sharing), and how the pattern integrates with storage and evaluation infrastructure.

mainPoints.point: Clarify once, then learn the default: the right fix is to ask, store, and silently apply later.
mainPoints.explanation: When a ParsedQuestion field is ambiguous, the system should ask one focused clarification, record the user's answer as a learned default, and apply it automatically in future equivalent queries.

mainPoints.point: Two Pydantic schemas formalize the loop: ClarificationRequest and ClarificationDefault.
mainPoints.explanation: ClarificationRequest is emitted for each missing field; ClarificationDefault tracks candidate values, weighted votes, and confidence. A gate function decides based on confidence whether to ask, apply silently, or ask occasionally.

mainPoints.point: Learned defaults are stratified on failure detection to handle edge cases.
mainPoints.explanation: When a default value fails (returns null), the system falls back to asking and then refines the default by adding sub-conditions (e.g., page 1 kind), improving future accuracy.

mainPoints.point: The pattern reduces user friction over time: easy questions become silent, only ambiguous ones trigger clarifications.
mainPoints.explanation: With confidence thresholds (below 0.6 always ask, above 0.85 apply silently), the system learns which defaults are reliable and stops bothering the user for predictable cases.

keyQuotes: The cheap fix is to ask. The right fix is to ask, then learn the default so the next case is silent.
Without the learned-default table, silent inference is just guessing.
The cost is two schemas and one table column. The benefit is that the system stops asking the easy questions and only asks the ambiguous ones.

relatedArticles.title: Stop Treating AI Memory Like a Search Problem
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article critiques the conventional 'store-and-retrieve' approach to AI memory, proposing a lifecycle-based system with decay, contradiction detection, confidence scoring, compression, and expiry to manage memory like a human brain rather than a static archive.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-5.5: A New Class of Intelligence for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces GPT-5.5, a new model designed for complex goal understanding and autonomous task completion, now available in ChatGPT and Codex.

relatedArticles.title: Your ReAct Agent Is Wasting 90% of Its Retries — Here’s How to Stop It
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article identifies a critical architectural flaw in ReAct-style LLM agents where hallucinated tool names waste the majority of retry budgets, and proposes three structural fixes—error taxonomy, per-tool circuit breakers, and deterministic tool routing—to eliminate this waste and improve production reliability.

relatedArticles.title: Embeddings Aren’t Magic: The Predictable Failure Modes of RAG Retrieval
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically debunks the magic of embeddings in RAG systems, demonstrating through reproducible experiments that embeddings excel at public vocabulary tasks but predictably fail on enterprise-specific terms, negation, magnitudes, and answer relevance, advocating for upstream filtering over stronger models.

relatedArticles.title: Building an Evaluation Harness for Production AI Agents: A 12-Metric Framework From 100+ Deployments
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a comprehensive 12-metric evaluation framework for production AI agents, distilled from over 100 enterprise deployments, covering retrieval, generation, agent behavior, and production health.

relatedArticles.title: Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful ChatGPT
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces a major upgrade to ChatGPT's memory system, using a more scalable 'dreaming' architecture that automatically synthesizes memories from chat history to improve freshness, continuity, and relevance.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing workspace agents in ChatGPT
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces workspace agents, a new class of shared, long-running AI agents within ChatGPT for business teams, designed to automate complex workflows, integrate with organizational tools, and operate under enterprise-grade controls.

relatedArticles.title: Hybrid Search and Re-Ranking in Production RAG
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a production-grade approach to improving RAG retrieval quality by combining hybrid search (BM25 + dense vectors) with cross-encoder re-ranking and metadata filtering, supported by real-world evaluation metrics.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces GPT-5.5, a new category of AI that acts as an autonomous agent capable of planning, reasoning, and executing complex multi-step tasks across different applications.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5, a generally available Mythos-class model with state-of-the-art capabilities, alongside Claude Mythos 5 for trusted cybersecurity partners, with new safeguards to mitigate misuse risks.
